Recommended Highlights This Week

1. Another Coffee Festival 2026 – 3–6 September, Guoco Tower Urban Park

2. Peppa Pig Fun Day Out – 5–6 September, Esplanade Theatre

3. Tembusu opens – 3 September, Singapore Botanic Gardens

4. Singapore Night Festival – final weekend, 4–5 September

5. SLA25 Rediscovery Trail continues – through 13 September

F&B Promotions

Current dining promotions across our Shangri-La Group properties in Singapore:

Shangri-La Singapore

Beng Hiang brings nearly 48 years of Hokkien heritage to the Garden Terrace, with recipes passed down from the original Chinatown shophouse. Signatures worth flagging to guests include Orh Nee (yam paste dessert) and Hae Bee Hiam (spicy dried shrimp sambal) – dishes that rarely appear on hotel menus outside a genuine Hokkien kitchen.

  • Beng Hiang – Authentic Hokkien Cuisine, Garden Terrace. Nearly 48-year-old recipes from the original Chinatown shophouse.

Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa

  • Rasa Private Beach BBQ – SGD 188++ per package (2 adults + 2 children). Valid through 31 December 2026.

Hotel Jen Tanglin

  • J65 – International Seafood Dinner Buffet returns to its standard rotation. $88++/adult, $44++/child. Shangri-La Circle members: 20% off.

Hotel Jen Orchard Gateway

  • Makan@JEN – daily lunch and dinner buffet, $30–55++ per person. 15% off for OCBC cardmembers, ongoing.

Overall Summary

Singapore Night Festival closes out its third and final weekend (4–5 September), capping off a strong run – worth one last push to any guest who hasn't been yet. The week's genuine new openings are worth flagging directly: Another Coffee Festival brings 34 specialty roasters from nine countries to Guoco Tower Urban Park for a free, booth-hopping tasting format; Tembusu opens inside the Botanic Gardens with a menu built around the actual 200-year-old Tembusu tree the restaurant is named for; and Peppa Pig makes her Singapore stage debut at Esplanade Theatre for the September school holidays. The SLA25 Rediscovery Trail also continues through 13 September – a genuinely good free option for guests who enjoy heritage and hidden corners of the city, and it connects directly to our own Alkaff Mansion recommendation.

Events & Festivals

Another Coffee Festival 2026

Singapore's first major industry-led specialty coffee festival, founded by two well-known names in the local coffee scene – Leon Foo of MORNING and Will Leow of Alchemist – through their non-profit Another Coffee Initiative. What sets it apart from a typical food festival is the format: rather than buying full drinks, guests purchase a reusable festival cup and tasting tokens, then move between 34 roasters sampling 70–80ml pours at a time. It brings together 19 Singapore-based roasters alongside 15 international names from nine countries, including Fuglen (Norway), Center Coffee (South Korea) and Coffee County (Japan) – several making their Singapore debut.

Event Date: 3–6 September 2026

Time: 11:00am–8:00pm (3–4 Sep), 10:00am–8:00pm (5–6 Sep)

Location: Guoco Tower Urban Park, 1 Wallich Street (directly above Tanjong Pagar MRT)

Admission: Free entry; festival cup and tasting token bundles from $21.60

Website: anothercoffee.sg

Best For: Coffee Enthusiasts / Couples / Something Different / Pet Owners (pet-friendly venue)

Concierge Recommendation: A genuinely good pick for guests who care about coffee, not just want to walk past a booth – the tasting-token format specifically rewards slowing down and talking to the roasters, so encourage guests not to rush through it.

SLA25 Rediscovery Trail

To mark the Singapore Land Authority's 25th anniversary, this free self-guided trail unlocks 25 State-managed properties across the island for public exploration – many of them buildings guests would otherwise walk straight past without knowing their history. The trail spans heritage and colonial buildings, lifestyle clusters, and green spaces, including Dempsey, New Bahru, Lau Pa Sat, Gillman Barracks, Lazarus Island, St John's Island, Chip Bee Gardens, and 195 Pearl's Hill Terrace – a former colonial police barracks now reimagined as an indie arts enclave. A mobile web app (no download required) tracks GPS-verified check-ins at each stop, with participants unlocking one of eight limited-edition digital mementos for every three properties visited, plus access to more than 140 exclusive tenant promotions along the way.

Event Date: 14 July – 13 September 2026

Location: 25 State properties islandwide

Admission: Free

Website: sla25trail.sla.gov.sg

Best For: Culture Seekers / History Buffs / Families / Free Activities

Concierge Recommendation: This connects directly to our own Alkaff Mansion recommendation, which is one of the 25 stops – a good way to introduce guests to the trail through a place we already recommend. For guests without much time, suggest starting with Dempsey or Lau Pa Sat, since both are easy to fold into a trip they'd likely make anyway.

Peppa Pig Fun Day Out! – Singapore Debut

Peppa Pig makes her official Singapore stage debut for the September school holidays, in an interactive live production designed specifically as a first theatre experience for toddlers and preschoolers. Rather than a traditional sit-and-watch show, the format encourages children to sing, dance and play along as Peppa, George, Mummy Pig and Daddy Pig head off on an adventure to the zoo and beach, complete with giant sandcastles, hungry penguins and Peppa's signature muddy puddles.

Event Date: 5–6 September 2026

Time: 5 Sep – 10:30am, 2:00pm & 5:30pm; 6 Sep – 10:30am & 2:00pm

Location: Esplanade Theatre, 1 Esplanade Drive, Singapore 038981

Admission: $28–$138 via SISTIC (VIP includes a post-show meet-and-greet with Peppa and friends)

Best For: Families with Toddlers & Preschoolers

Concierge Recommendation: A strong pick for families with very young children specifically – it's designed as a gentle introduction to live theatre, so it's a better fit than a typical concert or show for the 2–5 age range. This is a one-weekend-only run, so encourage early booking.

Singapore Night Festival – Final Weekend

Singapore Night Festival closes out its third and final weekend of the year. For full background on the festival, see Editions 008 and 009.

Event Date: 4–5 September 2026 (final weekend)

Location: Bras Basah.Bugis precinct, centred on the National Museum of Singapore

Admission: Free for most programmes

Concierge Recommendation: Last call for any guest who hasn't been – after this weekend, it won't return until next year's edition.

Restaurants & Bars

Tembusu

A new “Borderless Straits” dining concept from Fleursophy Group founder Nicole Chen, opening inside the Ginger Garden of the Singapore Botanic Gardens – Singapore's only UNESCO World Heritage Site. The name isn't decorative: the restaurant is named for the native Tembusu tree, which appears on the reverse of Singapore's five-dollar note, and the Gardens' own best-known Tembusu specimen – visible from parts of the grounds – is estimated to be more than 200 years old. The menu draws on cuisines from across the Straits of Malacca region without being tied to one single tradition.

Location: 1 Cluny Road, Singapore Botanic Gardens (Ginger Garden)

Opening: Soft-opened 3 August 2026; official launch 3 September 2026

Hours: Daily, main menu served 8:00am–9:00pm

Best For: Couples / Nature Lovers / Something Different / Garden Setting

Concierge Recommendation: A distinctive setting for a guest wanting to combine a Botanic Gardens visit with a genuinely good meal rather than a standard cafe – the tree connection is a nice detail to mention, since most guests won't know the significance of the name otherwise.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Jumbo Seafood

Founded in 1987 at East Coast Seafood Centre, Jumbo Seafood has grown into one of Singapore's most recognisable home-grown restaurant names, credited by many as the benchmark for the country's unofficial national dish. The restaurant's Dempsey outlet brings the same award-winning Chilli Crab and Black Pepper Crab to a leafier, more relaxed setting than the original East Coast branch, with additional signatures like Fried Prawns with Cereal and Crispy Baby Squid rounding out the menu.

Current Promotion: None advertised – check for seasonal crab promotions.

Reservation Policy: Strongly recommended, especially Friday and weekend dinners; no credit card required to book.

Contact: +65 6479 3435

Address: 11 Dempsey Road, #01-16, Singapore 249673

Website: jumboseafood.com.sg

Concierge Recommendation: If a guest asks for “the” Singapore chilli crab experience and hasn't already committed to a specific restaurant, this is a safe, very well-known default – remind them to book ahead, as walk-ins are genuinely risky on weekends.

Ce La Vi

Perched atop Marina Bay Sands' SkyPark, Ce La Vi is Southeast Asia's best-known rooftop restaurant and bar, 57 floors above the city with an open-air view that takes in the full Marina Bay skyline. The menu leans into contemporary Asian fusion – dishes like Silverfern Beef Tenderloin Tartare and Short Rib Bossam sit alongside more familiar international plates – but the main draw for most guests is the setting itself, particularly around sunset.

Current Promotion: None advertised.

Reservation Policy: Reservations strongly recommended, especially for sunset slots and the SkyBar side; no credit card required for standard dining bookings.

Contact: +65 6508 2188

Address: 1 Bayfront Avenue, Marina Bay Sands, Hotel Tower 3, Singapore 018971

Website: celavi.com/en/singapore

Concierge Recommendation: Book the sunset slot specifically if a guest wants the iconic photo – the view during the day is pleasant but nowhere near as memorable as watching the skyline light up from that height.

Hotel & Hospitality News

No new hotel or leadership announcements to report this week – all previously featured properties remain unchanged. Colleagues should continue monitoring for updates ahead of NoMad Singapore's late-2026 opening.

Transport & Operational Updates

Downtown Line Returns to Normal Hours

The Downtown Line's Friday night early closures and Saturday late starts, running since 10 July for engineering works, are scheduled to end by 5 September. Services should return to normal hours from this point onward – confirm with LTA channels if guests ask, since exact restoration timing can shift slightly.

Bras Basah.Bugis & Tanjong Pagar Crowds

Expect heavier foot traffic around Bras Basah.Bugis on 4–5 September (Singapore Night Festival's final weekend) and around Tanjong Pagar / Guoco Tower from 3–6 September (Another Coffee Festival).

7th Month Festival and Dinner – Truro Road

A temple community event will close Truro Road (between Lamp Post 3 and Lamp Post 5) on 3 September, 5:00pm–11:00pm, organised by Ling Ci Xing Gong temple as part of Hungry Ghost Festival observances. A small, localised closure, but worth knowing if a guest's route passes through the area that evening.

Overnight Works – Fort Canning Tunnel & PIE/TPE Slip Roads

Fort Canning Tunnel closes overnight (12:01am–5:00am) on 2 and 4 September for system testing, with traffic diverted via Stamford Road and Orchard Road. Separately, slip roads connecting Tampines Ave 7/Loyang Ave to the TPE and PIE will close overnight (10:00pm–5:30am) on various nights between 1 and 5 September for bridge works. Both are late-night closures unlikely to affect most guests, but worth knowing for anyone with a very early or overnight airport transfer that week.

Hungry Ghost Festival Continues

The Hungry Ghost Festival continues through 10 September. Guests may still notice incense, joss paper offerings and getai performances around the island; see Edition 007 for full background if the team needs a refresher.

Changi Airport Travel Advisory

Airport traffic remains elevated as the September school holiday period begins. Morning and weekend flights need extra buffer time for check-in, immigration and bag drop.

Looking Ahead

Singapore Gallery Month & SLA25 Trail – Final Stretch

Both Singapore Gallery Month and the SLA25 Rediscovery Trail close on 13 September – worth a final push in the next edition before both wrap up.

September School Holidays

The September school holiday period brings a wave of family-oriented programming across the city – expect more announcements in the coming weeks beyond Peppa Pig's debut this week.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Singapore Night Festival ends this weekend (4–5 September) – make this the final, direct nudge rather than a passing mention.

  • Peppa Pig Fun Day Out is a one-weekend-only run – encourage guests with young children to book promptly rather than wait.

  • Tembusu's official launch is 3 September, though it has been soft-open since early August – guests visiting from the 3rd onward should expect the full menu and experience.

  • The SLA25 Rediscovery Trail pairs naturally with our Alkaff Mansion recommendation – mention the connection when guests ask about either.

Suggested Itineraries

Half Day — Coffee & Culture

Afternoon: Another Coffee Festival at Guoco Tower Urban Park – buy a festival bundle and work through a few roasters at a relaxed pace.

Evening: Walk to nearby Tanjong Pagar for dinner, or continue on to Chinatown for an SLA25 Rediscovery Trail stop at 195 Pearl's Hill Terrace.

Tip: The coffee festival uses a token system, not individual purchases – explain this to guests before they arrive so they're not caught out expecting to buy drinks directly.

Full Day — Gardens, Heritage & Dinner

Morning: Singapore Botanic Gardens, ending with lunch at Tembusu in the Ginger Garden.

Afternoon: SLA25 Rediscovery Trail stop at Dempsey – easy to combine with shopping and browsing.

Evening: Dinner at Jumbo Seafood, also in Dempsey – no need to arrange separate transport between stops.

Tip: Dempsey ties together three separate recommendations in one afternoon – a genuinely efficient half-day for guests without much time.

2 Days — Family Weekend

Day 1

Morning: Gardens by the Bay. Afternoon: Rest before the evening. Evening: Ce La Vi for sunset drinks and dinner (adults), or an early dinner nearby with kids.

Day 2

Morning: SLA25 Rediscovery Trail family-friendly stops. Afternoon: Peppa Pig Fun Day Out at Esplanade Theatre (if travelling with young children and dates align).

Tip: Peppa Pig only runs 5–6 September – confirm this fits the guest's stay dates before building an itinerary around it.

Quick Reference

Best New Festival: Another Coffee Festival 2026

Best Free Heritage Activity: SLA25 Rediscovery Trail

Best Family Show: Peppa Pig Fun Day Out

Best New Restaurant: Tembusu

Best Classic Singapore Dining: Jumbo Seafood

Best Skyline Dining: Ce La Vi
